target.title: fix: builds stop hanging on stalled plugin asset hooks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where local builds, source CLI rebuilds, macOS restarts, Docker builds, CI, or release jobs could hang indefinitely when a bundled plugin asset build or copy hook stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each plugin-owned asset hook now has a 10-minute deadline, matching existing build and release command ceilings. Asset hooks remain shell command strings, so the deadline runs through the repository's managed-child owner: a detached process group on POSIX and `taskkill /T /F` on Windows. Timeout cleanup therefore terminates the shell and its descendants instead of only the shell leader. Timeout errors identify only the phase and plugin id, without forwarding child error details.

## User Impact

Developers and release operators now get a bounded, actionable failure instead of an indefinitely blocked build or a timeout that leaves plugin work running in the background. Successful Browser, Canvas, Diffs, and Discord asset generation keeps the existing commands and output behavior.

## Evidence

Exact head: `4b5de0afcd54e826f57b0c6cffea1dd209c07b34`

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/bundled-plugin-assets.test.ts test/scripts/managed-child-process.test.ts` — 18/18 passed. These tests run real child trees: the asset-hook regression starts a shell-owned launcher plus a descendant that ignores `SIGTERM`, and the shared managed-child regression verifies both parent and descendant are gone after the deadline. Existing Windows coverage verifies timeout cleanup's tree primitive uses `taskkill /T /F`.

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  18 passed (18)
  Duration  2.44s (transform 210ms, setup 95ms, import 126ms, tests 1.73s, environment 0ms)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 10.43s
```

- Real successful path: `node scripts/bundled-plugin-assets.mjs --phase build --plugin discord` completed successfully; generated SDK SHA-256: `72a78cd678dada982e7109aa31488f1c7cd85ad76e933e0d080a0bd9cf6ac6c7`.
- The managed-child `.d.mts` contract now exposes the same optional `timeoutMs` accepted by the runtime implementation.
- `oxfmt --check` for all five changed files — passed.
- Targeted Oxlint for the changed runtime/tests passed with the pre-existing `typescript/require-array-sort-compare` diagnostic on the unchanged alias-sort line allowed for this focused run.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --dry-run` selects the expected `testRoot` and `tooling` lanes. Exact-head GitHub CI supplies the clean-install full-lane proof.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound gh-read GitHub CLI execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where maintainers and repository automation using `scripts/gh-read` could hang indefinitely when the delegated GitHub CLI process stopped responding. A stalled read command could therefore block the surrounding workflow without returning an actionable failure.

- **Root cause:** `scripts/gh-read` owns the lifetime of every delegated `gh` child, but its canonical `runGitHubCli` boundary previously supplied no deadline.
- **Legal and error states:** Commands that finish within the selected finite owner budget preserve their existing behavior. Commands that exceed it fail with `ETIMEDOUT` and `SIGKILL` instead of hanging indefinitely; intentionally long-lived reads can select a larger validated budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

What is the intended outcome?

Root-cause fix: every delegated `gh` child started by `scripts/gh-read` has a finite validated owner-controlled lifetime, including long-lived commands whose operator selects a larger finite budget.

What should reviewers focus on?

`runGitHubCli` is the single source boundary for delegated child execution after token creation. Applying the deadline there protects every `gh-read` command rather than adding caller-specific checks or a drifting subcommand taxonomy. This is a root-cause fix, not a fallback or mitigation.

- **Timeout selection:** A representative healthy 5,000-PR pagination read took 52.816 seconds. A 30-second deadline would reject that legal path, 60 seconds would leave only about 7.2 seconds of margin, and 120 seconds leaves about 67.2 seconds. The two-minute value also matches the broad-pagination script-owner pattern merged in #109968.
- **Contract surface:** This changes only the repository `scripts/gh-read` wrapper and adds one documented optional environment control, `OPENCLAW_GH_READ_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`. It accepts a positive safe-integer millisecond value, defaults to `120000`, and does not change any OpenClaw product API, schema, protocol, or migration. Existing callers that do not set it keep the same default introduced by this PR; successful commands and ordinary nonzero statuses remain compatible.
- **Related open PR scan:** #110601 is a sibling timeout pattern for distinct scripts and call sites, not a competing implementation of the `gh-read` owner fix.
- **Out of scope:** The unchanged GitHub App token bootstrap, GitHub API fetch handling, and other direct `execPlainGh` or `execFileSync` call sites are intentionally not changed. The wrapper does not infer timeout policy from specific `gh` subcommand names.
- **Risk explanation:** A legitimate command longer than the selected budget will be terminated, and an operator can choose a value that is unnecessarily short or long.
- **Why acceptable:** The default has measured headroom for broad pagination, long-lived commands can choose an explicit finite budget, and invalid values fail before spawning `gh`. Token propagation, authentication, secret handling, inherited stdio, successful exits, and ordinary failure statuses are unchanged.

## User Impact

Maintainers and repository automation now receive an actionable `ETIMEDOUT` failure instead of waiting forever when a delegated GitHub CLI command stalls. Healthy ordinary commands keep the two-minute default, while intentionally long-lived reads such as `gh run watch` can set `OPENCLAW_GH_READ_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` to a larger finite value.

## Evidence

- Exact tested candidate tree was committed unchanged as `32a4b05c80a711ff3b6037bdc6fb34763ebb3785`.
- Real stalled-child proof through the exact production `runGitHubCli` owner used a real `spawnSync` child and the default process options. It completed after 120,105 ms with:

  ```json
  {"timeout":120000,"killSignal":"SIGKILL","error":"ETIMEDOUT","status":null,"signal":"SIGKILL"}
  ```

- Real operator-override proof through the same production owner selected a 5,000 ms finite budget and allowed a real child to complete with status 0 after 2,020 ms.
- Representative healthy pagination through the same production owner ran `gh pr list -R openclaw/openclaw --state merged --limit 5000 --json author --jq length`. The command printed `5000` with status 0 in 49,452 ms, leaving more than 70 seconds of margin below the two-minute default.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/gh-read.test.ts` — 18/18 passed.
- Targeted Oxlint for `scripts/gh-read.ts` and `test/scripts/gh-read.test.ts` — passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 scripts/gh-read.ts test/scripts/gh-read.test.ts docs/help/scripts.md` — passed.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- The runtime proofs exercised the changed delegated-command boundary with a real child and a live GitHub query. This environment did not have the GitHub App ID/private key required to repeat the unchanged outer installation-token bootstrap, so that external credential gap remains explicitly disclosed.
